title: Create a Project and Navigate Trackers Knowledge Check

questions.question: What permission does a user need in order to create a new Codebeamer project?
options: Project Admin role within an existing project
questions.rationale: Creating a new project requires Create Project group permissions, which is a system-level permission, not a role within a specific project. The Project Admin role applies once a project exists. Trackers - Administrate and Developer role membership control access within an existing project's trackers, not project creation.

questions.question: When creating a default (blank) project, which field is required to uniquely identify the project?
questions.rationale: Name is the required field that uniquely identifies a project. Category is optional and defaults to 'Uncategorized' if not specified. Image and Membership constraints are optional configuration settings, not required identifiers.

questions.question: A JAWS team member wants any user to be able to request access to the proof-of-concept project, but a Project Admin should approve each request before access is granted. Which membership visibility setting should be used?
questions.rationale: Public with approval allows any user to request to join, but requires a project administrator to approve each request. Public allows automatic joining with no approval step. Private requires administrators to add members directly with no self-service requests. 'Available as template' is unrelated to membership visibility - it controls whether other projects can reuse this project's configuration.

questions.question: Where are permissions configured for members of a Codebeamer project?
options: Individually for each member on the Members page
At the role level, by editing the role's permissions
Individually for each group added to the project
Only through the Tracker Permissions tab
questions.rationale: Permissions are edited at the role level - you cannot edit permissions for an individual member or group directly. Members and groups are assigned to roles, and all members of a role share that role's permission set. The Tracker Permissions tab configures permissions for a specific tracker by role, which is a finer-grained layer on top of project-level role permissions.

questions.question: In the Configuration Diagram, what do blue Generalization arrows represent?
options: Inheritance from a derived tracker to its template tracker
A reference from a declaring field to a target tracker
The order in which trackers appear in the Tracker Tree
questions.rationale: Blue Generalization arrows show inheritance, pointing from a derived tracker to the template tracker it is based on. Bi-directional traceability between trackers is shown with regular arrows representing references, and references from a declaring field to target trackers are shown as light blue arrows. The Tracker Tree order is independent of, and does not affect, the Configuration Diagram.
